title: No unit test for exported SeedOrders() function
description: SeedOrders() is an exported function and the canonical data fixture for /api/orders. It has no dedicated unit test. TestOrdersHandler_GET only asserts len > 0, so a mutation of SeedOrders() (wrong count, wrong status) would not be caught. The handlers_test.go file acknowledges this as seeded defect SD-07 (lines 50-57).
recommended_action: Add TestSeedOrders that calls SeedOrders() directly and asserts exact count (3) and expected field values for each Order struct.

title: json.Encoder error branch in OrdersHandler has 0% coverage
evidence: Coverage profile: orders.go:47.3,49.1 2 0 (hit count = 0). Lines: if err := json.NewEncoder(w).Encode(orders); err != nil { http.Error(w, "internal server error", http.StatusInternalServerError); return }
description: The JSON encode error path (HTTP 500 response) inside OrdersHandler has never been executed by any test. httptest.NewRecorder's Write() never fails, so the branch is unreachable without injecting a broken ResponseWriter. The error path is dead in all current tests.
recommended_action: Create a failing ResponseWriter that returns an error from Write(), pass it to OrdersHandler, and assert the response code is 500.

title: No test for GET /health route — route is absent and untested
evidence:
// SD-01: GET /health is required by docs/release-runbook.md section 3.1 and FR-32 but is deliberately NOT registered here.
func NewRouter() http.Handler { mux := http.NewServeMux(); mux.HandleFunc("/api/orders", OrdersHandler); mux.HandleFunc("/ready", ReadinessHandler); return loggingMiddleware(mux) }
description: The router explicitly notes that /health is intentionally omitted (SD-01). There is no test that sends GET /health through the router and verifies HTTP 200. Without such a test, the missing route is invisible to the test suite.
recommended_action: Add TestNewRouter_HealthRoute that sends GET /health through NewRouter() and asserts HTTP 200 with JSON body {"status":"ok"}. The test will fail until the handler and route are added.

title: cmd/server/main.go has 0.0% test coverage — entire entry point untested
description: There are no test files in sample-app/cmd/server/. Env-var defaulting (PORT, DB_DSN, LOG_LEVEL), server construction, graceful shutdown, and signal handling are all untested. Total cross-package statement coverage is dragged down by this gap.
recommended_action: Extract server configuration and construction into a testable helper function in a non-main file. Add TestBuildServer to verify address, timeouts, and handler wiring. Use an integration test with httptest.NewServer to cover the startup path.

title: OrdersHandler function-level coverage is 81.8% due to uncovered error branch
evidence:
go test -cover ./...
handlers coverage: 94.4%
OrdersHandler: 81.8% (lines 47-49, hit count 0)
description: OrdersHandler reports 81.8% function-level coverage. The two uncovered statements are inside the json.Encode error guard (same root cause as TC-002). The 94.4% package-level metric masks this gap.
recommended_action: Same fix as TC-002: inject a failing ResponseWriter to trigger the error branch and bring OrdersHandler to 100%.

title: TestOrdersHandler_GET does not assert exact order count or field values
evidence: if len(orders) == 0 { t.Fatal("expected at least one order in response") }
description: The test only checks len > 0. If SeedOrders() were changed to return a single empty Order{}, this test would still pass. There is no assertion on the exact count (3), IDs, customer names, statuses, or other fields.
recommended_action: Assert len(orders) == 3 and compare each order against the values returned by SeedOrders(), or use reflect.DeepEqual between the decoded response and SeedOrders().

title: Method-not-allowed tests only cover POST, not PUT/PATCH/DELETE
description: Both TestReadinessHandler_MethodNotAllowed and TestOrdersHandler_MethodNotAllowed test only POST. Methods like PUT, PATCH, DELETE are not explicitly verified, leaving the 405 contract partially documented.
recommended_action: Use table-driven tests iterating over []string{http.MethodPost, http.MethodPut, http.MethodPatch, http.MethodDelete} and asserting 405 for each.

title: TestReadinessHandler_GET does not assert Content-Type header
description: TestOrdersHandler_GET asserts Content-Type: application/json, but TestReadinessHandler_GET does not, even though readiness.go sets it explicitly. Removing the header from the handler would not be caught.
recommended_action: Add: ct := resp.Header.Get("Content-Type"); if ct != "application/json" { t.Fatalf(...) }
